title: Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, Sol and Luna added to alphaflowseven
author: engineering-AF7
selftext:
This is how it works in one of the signal types, named "Team"

You name two to five AI traders and give each one its own model. Then they talk.

**How a team meeting works**

* Every member reads the same market data and posts its opening position to a shared message board.
* Over one to three discussion rounds, they reply to each other by name. They challenge weak arguments and change their minds when the evidence says so.
* Then every member votes BUY, SELL, HOLD or CLOSE, with a conviction score and a trade plan. The votes are counted by code, not by a model. The majority wins, a tie goes to the side with more total conviction, and a deadlock is a HOLD.

**They keep talking between meetings**

The board doesn't close when the meeting ends. If a member is addressed by name, it wakes up and replies. A member that sees the market moving can ask for an early meeting. A Team Desk seat watches the open trade between meetings and posts its reasoning to the board. You can read the whole conversation in the Team Room.

**They record their thoughts**

Each member keeps a journal, a running record of what it thought and did that it can never erase. It also keeps a notebook of up to 30 short notes it chooses to hold on to. Both come back to the member at every meeting, so it remembers what it argued last week and how that turned out.

Members can also rewrite their own personal instructions as they learn. Every version is kept, so you can compare, revert or lock them. The team's ground rules stay fixed.

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body:
The conviction tiebreaker seems worth testing separately from the discussion rounds. With two to five traders using different models, one member's 90 might mean the same thing as another's 60. Counting votes in code makes the procedure deterministic, but doesn't make those scores comparable.

For tied BUY/SELL votes, I'd check how often the winner changes when each member's conviction is replaced by its percentile within its own past scores. Frequent flips would show that score scale is driving the result. Are conviction scores calibrated per member, especially after it rewrites its personal instructions?
